audits.title: 199 Improving Timeliness and Availability of Bariatric MDT Outcomes on Electronic Patient Records: A Quality Improvement Initiative
audits.setting: Bariatric MDT, Whittington University Hospital, London

cycle1.result: 227 (15.3%) had no MDT outcome on EPR; of 1272 with a report, 8.5% (n=108) same-day entries; average delay 36 days (range 0–550).

audits.intervention: Live documentation of MDT outcomes during the meeting from January 2025.

cycle2.result: 11 (3.7%) lacked an EPR report; of 279, 43.4% (n=121) same-day entries; average delay 3.8 days (range 0–121).

audits.citation: Attarde S, Gasimov M, Sufi P, Younus H. 199 Improving Timeliness and Availability of Bariatric MDT Outcomes on Electronic Patient Records: A Quality Improvement Initiative. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_17). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf270.216.

audits.title: Multidisciplinary cancer care in Australia: a national audit highlights gaps in care and medico-legal risk for clinicians.
audits.standard: Best practice and national recommendations for multidisciplinary cancer care
audits.setting: 155 hospitals across Australia, five cancer types

cycle1.result: Two-thirds of hospitals had no multidisciplinary team; of those with a team, one-third did not inform patients of discussion, half did not seek consent for all cases, one-quarter did not record the recommended plan in the notes.

audits.other_findings: Less than 1% of teams reported routine attendance by the tumour-specific minimum core team.
audits.citation: Wilcoxon H, Luxford K, Saunders C, Peterson J, Zorbas H, National Breast and Ovarian Cancer Centre's Multidisciplinary Care Audit Steering Committee. Multidisciplinary cancer care in Australia: a national audit highlights gaps in care and medico-legal risk for clinicians. Asia Pac J Clin Oncol. 2011;7(1):34-40. doi:10.1111/j.1743-7563.2010.01369.x. PMID: 21332649.

audits.title: Clinical audit of multidisciplinary care at a medium-sized hospital in Spain.
audits.standard: National recommendations for multidisciplinary cancer care
audits.setting: Medium-sized hospital, Hospital Universitario Puerta de Hierro-Majadahonda, Madrid

cycle1.result: 64.5% discussed at a cancer conference at some point, but only 40% had documented MDT discussion before first treatment; pathological stage documented in 53.6%.

audits.other_findings: 77 conferences observed; nine teams met weekly or biweekly with average ten attendees and six specialties, mean duration 46.8 min; nursing input lacking.
audits.citation: Ruiz-Casado A, Ortega MJ, Soria A, Cebolla H. Clinical audit of multidisciplinary care at a medium-sized hospital in Spain. World J Surg Oncol. 2014;12:53. doi:10.1186/1477-7819-12-53. PMID: 24597686.

audits.title: Enhancing Documentation of Upper Limb Specialist Team Meetings at a Tertiary Trauma Centre.
audits.setting: Upper limb specialist team meeting, tertiary trauma centre (Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham)

cycle1.result: No complex patient outcomes were documented in the electronic patient record; outcomes were kept as PowerPoint slides in a shared folder.

audits.intervention: Structured documentation template, centralised storage and a shared worklist integrated into the clinical portal.

cycle2.result: 39/44 complex cases (89%) had outcomes recorded directly in the EPR through the shared worklist.

audits.other_findings: The five undocumented cases occurred during the junior doctor changeover period.
audits.citation: Mahajan U, Gadullah M, Rangan R, Memon K. Enhancing Documentation of Upper Limb Specialist Team Meetings at a Tertiary Trauma Centre. Cureus. 2025;17(11):e97169. doi:10.7759/cureus.97169. PMID: 41426846.

audits.title: Decision to delivery: do vascular MDT discussions achieve their intended clinical targets?
audits.standard: Final management should match the recorded MDT decision
audits.setting: Vascular MDT, Glan Clwyd Hospital, North Wales

cycle1.result: 39 of 278 (14%) MDT decisions deviated from the agreed plan; main causes surgical plan changes (33.3%) and patient unfitness (20.5%); 33.3% three-month mortality and major amputation among discrepancies.

cycle2.result: 48 of 443 (10.8%) deviated; system delays the leading cause (31.25%); three-month mortality and amputation fell to 29%.

audits.citation: Sargious AN, Taha WM, Zafar MA, Jararaa SA, Al-Zaghal AA, Roble AA, et al.. Decision to delivery: do vascular MDT discussions achieve their intended clinical targets?. Int Angiol. 2026;45(3):191-198. doi:10.23736/s0392-9590.26.05525-2. PMID: 41949985.
